messages:
alex: heads up — security detector flagged an S3 upload with no SSE metadata: s3://redwood-backups/prod/db-snap-2026-03-21-1. seeing Content-MD5 but no x-amz-server-side-encryption header. link: https://s3.console.aws/obj/backup-id-abc123
security-bot: [ALERT] ID: ALRT-20260321-42 — object lacks SSE header, matched policy rule 7.2. auto-tagged as unencrypted_snapshot.
priya: omg. which job uploaded this? can we tell the IAM principal?
alex: quick grep of access logs shows PutObject by arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/backup-agent-prod at 2026-03-21T18:22:09Z
jason: backup-agent-prod just had the role policy trimmed yesterday (rbac change) to allow cross-account writes for DR. wonder if we accidentally removed condition requiring kms:Encrypt.
maria: ^ good call. check CMK grants and the bucket policy too — maybe it fell back to plaintext when kms grant absent.
oncall-sre: running head-object and kms decrypt dry-run now. will paste outputs.
oncall-sre: `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-backups --key prod/db-snap-2026-03-21-1`
oncall-sre: output: {"ContentLength": 412345678, "Metadata": {"uploaded-by":"backup-agent"}} (no ServerSideEncryption field)
oncall-sre: kms decrypt attempted against our CMK for object key returns: "Error: InvalidCiphertextException" — object isn't encrypted with CMK.
priya: that confirms it. timeline: snapshot created 18:21Z, uploaded 18:22Z. who kicked the job? job id shows backup-agent v2.4.1.
jason: we shipped v2.4.1 with a minor IAM change yesterday — policy removed explicit kms:Encrypt in favor of broader s3:PutObject for cross-account. i bet the grant flow failed and agent defaulted to no-sse path.
alex: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) block writes from backup-agent role using temporary IAM restrict, 2) add a bucket policy deny for PutObject lacking x-amz-server-side-encryption, 3) mark object as sensitive and isolate.
maria: agree. also revoke any ephemeral creds issued to backup-agent during the window and rotate the agent service token.
priya: I'm going to open an incident in PagerDuty and assign to sec-ops + infra. setting incident: INC-2026-03-21-enc-snap.
security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-21-enc-snap. Severity: P2. Notifications sent to @sec-ops, @oncall-infra.
oncall-sre: applied temporary bucket policy deny (put object condition StringEquals: sse != AES256 && sse != aws:kms). confirmed subsequent PutObject calls failing as intended.
jason: rolling back yesterday RBAC change is risky at scale. prefer restricting role ability first then patch agent to require SSE and fail loudly.
alex: decision: do both — temp restrict role + patch agent to add explicit kms:Encrypt permission and client-side SSE enforcement.
maria: tasks: 1) PR to agent repo to add mandatory SSE header + 400 on missing SSE (owner: jason). 2) Temporary IAM policy change to deny PutObject for backup-agent unless sse conditions met (owner: priya). 3) Audit run to list objects uploaded without SSE in last 48h and snapshot ids (owner: alex). 4) Run restoration test for a random non-sensitive snapshot to validate restore path (owner: oncall-sre).
priya: for remediation of this object: we should not download and reupload plaintext. options: a) if original db still present, re-take snapshot via encrypted flow; b) if not, we need to treat it as sensitive and follow exposure playbook.
alex: DB is on primary cluster still — option (a) possible. schedule urgent encrypted snapshot for 19:00Z via maintenance window.
oncall-sre: started audit: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-backups --prefix prod/ --query 'Contents[?@.Size>0].Key'` then head-object each to check ServerSideEncryption. initial scan shows 7 objects without SSE in last 48h.
jason: excellent catch. we should also check KMS grants: if agent used an external cross-account grant but the grant expired, the agent might have retried without SSE flag. check CloudTrail for kms:GenerateDataKey calls around 18:22Z.
maria: adding to tasks: log retention tweak — ensure S3 PutObject events and KMS GenerateDataKey events are retained for 90 days in central audit account (owner: alex).
priya: mitigation notes for incident report: - blocked writes, - rotated agent creds, - scheduled agent patch, - started re-encrypted snapshot, - audit list produced, - incident owners assigned.
oncall-sre: I've revoked current temporary role session tokens issued in the last 2h for backup-agent-prod.
alex: we should also add automated canary that attempts a PutObject without SSE and asserts it's rejected; add to infra health checks (owner: jason).
jason: will open PR for canary. small code snippet for enforcement test: ```bash
curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" --data-binary @dummy.bin https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-backups/prod/canary-test || echo "expected failure"
```
maria: post-incident actions (postmortem agenda): 1) root cause (RBAC change + missing grant/agent fallback), 2) timeline, 3) gaps in audit alerting, 4) remediation completed + verification, 5) policy to require SSE by default in infra templates.
priya: incident assigned: owners set, will run postmortem tomorrow 11:00PT. tagging compliance for review.
alex: any objections to marking this as security incident with compliance notification?
maria: no objections — please notify compliance and legal.
priya: pinged compliance@redwood and legal@redwood.
security-bot: Auto-checklist appended: "Notify compliance", "Rotate service tokens", "Audit list attached".
alex: thanks everyone. small follow-ups: jason — patch + canary. priya — IAM/bucket changes + incident comms. oncall-sre — restore test and audit full list. i'll own the postmortem write-up.
jason: ack. starting PR now.
oncall-sre: restore test succeeded for encrypted re-snapshot at 19:07Z. 
priya: closing the live exposure window. remaining work moved to postmortem/action items.
maria: 👍 :white_check_mark:
alex: closing thread for live triage. postmortem link will be posted when ready.
